text:
**Overall:** 6.0/10

The code is small, readable, and has a solid pytest suite for the intended happy paths. I would not approve it as-is because the core ingestion/upsert path can silently corrupt accounting data in realistic re-ingest scenarios.

**Findings**

| Severity | Location | Issue |
|---|---:|---|
| high | [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70) 70-84 | Equal-rank terminal states overwrite each other without comparing record freshness, so an older `COMPLETED` row can replace a newer `FAILED` row. |
| high | [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:66) 66-80 | Re-ingest “unchanged” detection only compares `state`, `end`, and `elapsed_sec`, ignoring changed user, partition, start, submit, CPU/GPU allocation, and exit code. |
| medium | [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:118) 118-126; [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14) 14, 50-148 | Timezone-aware ISO timestamps are accepted but later compared as SQLite text, which gives incorrect chronological filtering when offsets differ. |
| medium | [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:148) 148-163 | Negative `AllocCPUS` and negative GPU counts are accepted, allowing negative CPU/GPU-hour reports. |
| medium | [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:121) 121-180; [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:52) 52-59 | Report commands call the same create-if-missing DB opener as ingest, so a typo in `--db` silently creates an empty database and returns empty reports. |
| medium | [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) 13-27; [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:50) 50-148 | The schema has no versioning/migration path and no indexes for reference-time, state, user, or partition report queries. |
| medium | [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:172) 172-194; [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:90) 90-103 | Ingest parses the entire dump into memory before writing, which is fragile for large `sacct` exports. |
| medium | [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:90) 90-103, 121-143, 172-180 | Only a narrow set of ingest errors is handled; permission, decode, SQLite, and corrupt DB errors escape as stack traces. |
| low | [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:152) 152-164 | Empty `User`, `Partition`, and `ExitCode` fields are accepted and stored, producing ambiguous report groups. |
| low | [jobwatch/__init__.py](/work/jobwatch/__init__.py:3) 3; [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:7) 7 | Version is duplicated between package metadata and runtime code, so releases can drift. |

**Estimate:** about 180 lines need rewrite or significant change, including production code and focused regression tests.

**Verification:** `python -m pytest -q` passed: 61 tests. `compileall` could not write `__pycache__` because the workspace is read-only for cache directories, and package build could not run because `build` is not installed.

**Bottom line:** No, I would not approve this as-is.

issues.description: Equal-rank terminal states overwrite each other without comparing record freshness.
Unchanged detection ignores changed user, partition, timestamps, allocation, GPU count, and exit code.
Timezone-aware timestamps are accepted but later compared lexicographically as text.
Negative CPU and GPU allocation values are accepted and can produce negative usage.
Report commands silently create a new empty database when the DB path is wrong.
Schema has no migrations or report-query indexes.
Ingest loads the full dump into memory before writing to SQLite.
Operational errors escape as stack traces instead of clean CLI failures.
Empty user, partition, and exit-code fields are accepted and stored.
Package version is duplicated and can drift between runtime and metadata.
